- [USER] I think I read somewhere that Conan Doyle didn't like writing Sherlock Holmes stories but just continued because they were so popular? Is that true?
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Sir Arthur Conan Doyle was initially somewhat ambivalent about the Sherlock Holmes stories and referred to them as a "lower stratum of literary achievement."
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Despite his reservations, he continued to write the stories, which became some of the most popular and enduring works of detective fiction.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Conan Doyle created Sherlock Holmes to supplement his income as a struggling young author, writing "A Study in Scarlet" in just three weeks.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The character became a cultural phenomenon after the publication of "The Adventures of Sherlock Holmes" in 1892.
